angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 425,281 km at 187.90 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.3219 +/- 0.0440 mas (same row, RUWE 3.21): 187.90 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.6113 +/- 0.008 solar radii from Bryant et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.533.3893B/abstract): 425,281 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.635 +/- 0.016 solar masses from Bryant et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.533.3893B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3943 +/- 14 K from Bryant et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.533.3893B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bryant et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2384 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.533.3893B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2384.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.668, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2384 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.332 dex, from Bryant et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.533.3893B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2384 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.11907, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2384 (pscomppars): age 9.4 Gyr, from Bryant et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.533.3893B/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
